conventions.q25: Q25 convention: linear interpolation between order statistics (numpy 'linear' / Excel PERCENTILE.INC default) -- h=(n-1)*0.25 over the sorted matured pool, value = s[floor(h)] + frac*(s[ceil(h)]-s[floor(h)]).
conventions.episode: Episode convention: a contiguous run of bad_t==True by adjacent quarter index (undefined/None quarters treated as not-bad for run-breaking purposes -- this only matters at series boundaries: T_REL's undefined stretch is the first ~20+12 quarters and fwd12's undefined stretch is the last 12, never a mid-series gap, so no episode is artificially split). An episode is 'caught' by a classifier if the classifier is True (defined-and-true) in any quarter from 4 quarters before the episode start through the episode's last quarter, inclusive.

honesty.contamination_note: v2's published results (cell medians, decade decay, C3 refutation) inform this design; the gate/targets/cuts are frozen before computing any 2x2 table. The known clustering of loss events (2006-08 US, 1990s JP) means OR estimates are dominated by few episodes; episode counts (distinct contiguous bad-spells caught vs missed) are reported alongside quarter counts for exactly this reason.
honesty.overlap_caveat: Overlap robustness: forward windows overlap (serial correlation inflates n). Report metrics on non-overlapping subsamples: every 12th quarter at offsets {0,4,8}, median OR of the offsets, with per-offset event counts. Small-n caveat flagged when a subsample has <10 usable quarters.

## Amendment 2 — 2026-07-14, warn-basis re-validation (from the design audit)
The design audit (scripts/compass_design_audit_charter.md; findings F1/C4) found
the supply-glut warn flag uses a TRAILING 24q z while a glut is arguably an
ABSOLUTE concept — with demonstrated warning fatigue (JP 2023Q3: vacancy 13.6%,
near the all-time high, reads trailing z −0.67 → warn OFF; MY 2022Q2 similar) —
and an internal inconsistency (the same series is EXPANDING in the report card).
warn is an input of the validated W_PRIM, so per audit charter §4 this cannot be
silently fixed; it is re-validated here.

Frozen rules:
- warn_exp: expanding robust z (ez(), same MAD/clamp/minobs=12 conventions as
  build_compass.py) on the SAME raw level series (vacancy, months-supply per
  market; US raw.months/raw.vac from clock-us.json), sign such that loose =
  negative, threshold ≤ −1, OR-combination — identical to trailing warn except
  the basis. No threshold or window search.
- W_PRIM_EXP = starved ∧ warn_exp. Evaluated with the IDENTICAL v3 machinery
  (both targets, gate, MH pooling, episode counts, overlap robustness).
- Decision rule (frozen): the live gauge switches to the expanding basis ONLY if
  W_PRIM_EXP passes the same ABS+REL gates AND its ABS MH-pooled OR ≥ the
  trailing version's. Otherwise trailing stays (status quo unless dominated),
  and the conceptual tension is published as a finding: the trailing warning
  works empirically even though a glut is conceptually absolute.
- Both versions' full tables are published regardless of outcome.
Timing disclosure: this amendment was written after the audit revealed the
fatigue cases but before any W_PRIM_EXP table was computed.

## Amendment 3 — 2026-07-14, adding Australia as an out-of-sample market (rule frozen before any AU number computed)
Australia is added to the clock as a 5th market AFTER the v3 risk claim was frozen
and published on {US, TW, MY, JP}. Frozen treatment (decided before any AU 2×2
table exists), so AU cannot be cherry-picked into or out of the headline:
- The PRIMARY validated claim stays EXACTLY as published: 4-market set, ABS on
  US+JP, MH pooled 13.53 / 16.07. These numbers are NOT restated with AU folded in.
- AU is evaluated with the identical v3 machinery (both targets, applicability
  gate, per-market 2×2/OR/precision/recall, episode analysis) and reported as a
  HOLD-OUT: the first market the warning meets that it was never fit to.
- A 5-market MH pooled OR is ALSO computed and shown, but LABELLED "with AU
  (out-of-sample)" and never substituted for the frozen 4-market figure.
- Applicability gate applies unchanged: AU is rated for ABS only if it has ≥8
  matured 3y-loss quarters. Prior expectation (disclosed, not a threshold): AU
  rarely posts multi-year nominal losses, so it will likely be NOT RATED for ABS
  and evaluated on REL only — an informative outcome either way, reported as-is.
- Whatever AU shows, the live clock's AU risk gauge uses the same per-market
  state logic already in place (WARNING ON/OFF where rated; NOT RATED / NOT
  VALIDATED shown honestly where not) — no new favourable framing invented for AU.
Adding AU does not alter any existing market's warn/quad/W_PRIM series (verified
by regression guard: the 4 markets' compass arrays must be byte-identical after
AU is wired into build_compass.py).

th_holdout.amendment_text_verbatim:
## Amendment 4 — 2026-07-31, adding Thailand (Bangkok) to the data layer (rule frozen before any Thai statistic in this block was computed)
Thailand is added as a 6th market AFTER the v3 risk claim was frozen and published on
{US, TW, MY, JP}, and after Australia was added as the first hold-out (Amendment 3).
Frozen treatment:
- The PRIMARY validated claim is unchanged: 4-market set, ABS on US+JP, MH pooled 13.53 / 16.07.
  Thailand does not enter it and no pooled figure is restated with Thailand folded in.
- The v3 RISK GAUGE IS NOT EVALUABLE for Thailand and is therefore NOT EVALUATED. The primary
  classifier W_PRIM = (quad == starved) AND (warn == true) requires the supply-glut term, and
  Thailand has no supply series at all: months and vacancy are 141/141 null because no official
  Thai quarterly inventory / absorption / vacancy series exists (REIC is an unextractable SPA;
  the private surveys are annual, begin ~2021 and disagree by more than 60% on the same
  "Greater Bangkok unsold units" concept). The glut term is UNDEFINED, not false, so W_PRIM
  cannot be formed. No proxy is substituted, no 2x2 table is computed, and the applicability
  gate is not applied. Thailand is NOT RATED for a stronger reason than Australia: Australia's
  gauge could be computed and merely lacked loss events to be rated on; Thailand's cannot be
  computed at all. build_compass.py encodes this as warn = null (never false) plus a market-level
  "supply_available": false, so that no renderer can show Thailand as "no supply-glut warning" —
  which would be a false negative, and would contradict this site's own /th/report (210,112
  unsold units, 49.5 months of stock).
- What IS evaluated is the Test-8 four-cell forward-return ordering (declared
  Fuelled >= Draining >= Reflating >= Starved), because it needs only momentum, credit and
  forward returns, all of which Thailand has across 1991-2026. Method, declared ordering and
  verdict thresholds are exactly those already applied to TW and AU in
  scripts/backtest_compass.py (rho >= 0.3 HOLDS, 0.1-0.3 WEAK, < 0.1 BREAKS); they were fixed
  before any Thai number was read and the result is published whichever way it falls, as
  Australia's rho = -0.156 BREAKS was.
- Adding Thailand does not alter any existing market's arrays (regression guard: the five
  existing markets' clock-*.json and compass-*.json are byte-identical after Thailand is wired
  into build_compass.py).
th_holdout.protocol_file_status: This amendment text is recorded in this JSON only. scripts/compass_v3_protocol.md was NOT edited in this pass (that file is outside the Thailand data-layer workstream's ownership); append this text verbatim as Amendment 4 when the protocol file is next touched.

risk_gauge.reason: W_PRIM = starved AND supply-glut; Thailand has zero supply data (months and vacancy 141/141 null), so the glut term is undefined and the classifier cannot be formed. This is structural, not a coverage gap that a retry fixes.
risk_gauge.distinct_from_au: AU is NOT RATED because its computable gauge had only 2 matured 3y-loss quarters against the >=8 gate. TH is NOT RATED because the gauge cannot be computed at all.

descriptive_only.note: Descriptive counts, NOT a gate evaluation (the gate is not applied because the classifier is undefined).

ordering_check.test: Test 8 -- declared four-cell ordering Fuelled >= Draining >= Reflating >= Starved
ordering_check.method: scripts/backtest_compass.py analyze() run unmodified on data/compass-th.json (the script's own MKTS list was not edited); quarter-level Spearman rho of declared cell rank (fuelled=4 .. starved=1) against realised fwd12 (3-year forward nominal price return), over every quarter with a non-null fwd12 and a non-warmup cell.
ordering_check.target: fwd12 = 3-year forward nominal Bangkok house-price return (BIS QTHN628BIS)
ordering_check.thresholds: rho >= 0.3 HOLDS; 0.1-0.3 WEAK; < 0.1 BREAKS (unchanged from the TW/AU runs)

supplementary_non_overlapping.note: SUPPLEMENTARY, not the headline: 3-year forward windows overlap, so the 111 scored quarters are far from independent. Every 12th quarter, offsets {0,4,8}, same rho convention. n is 9-10 per offset, so each is noisy.

current_quarter_state.note: 2026Q1 is warmup because BIS household credit ends 2025Q4 while BIS prices run to 2026Q1; the last credit value is deliberately NOT carried forward. The last COMPLETE compass reading is 2025Q4.

data_limitations: No supply data of any kind: months and vacancy are 141/141 null. warn is null, never false; the supply gauge has no value. Bangkok is in fact heavily oversupplied (site's own /th/report: 210,112 unsold units, 49.5 months), so a rendering that reads 'no glut' would be a false negative.
Credit ends 2025Q4 while prices end 2026Q1, so the compass credit axis and the current cell are null at 2026Q1; not imputed, not carried forward.

Valuation = price / income with income = ILOSTAT average monthly earnings PER EMPLOYEE (baht/worker/month), not household disposable income as for AU -- NOT unit-comparable across markets. Income starts 2014Q1 (2015Q1 dropped as an evident source unit error), so the first valuation z is 2017Q1 and the standardisation base is not full (24 obs) until ~2020Q1.
No pti: Thailand publishes no official price-to-income ratio.
price is the BIS BANGKOK city index, not a nationwide Thai index.

pop is the World Bank annual value stepped onto the quarterly axis (YoY at lag 4 is well defined; QoQ within a year is zero by construction); 2026Q1 null. Population peaked in 2022 and has declined since -- the negative population gauge is real.
unemp has seven missing COVID-era quarters (2020Q2, 2021Q1-2022Q3) and sits structurally near 1%, so small absolute moves dominate its z.
rate is spliced at 2000Q2/2000Q3 (money-market rate before, BOT policy rate after) with a ~0.48pp level step, so YoY across 2000Q3-2001Q2 is not clean.

The Structure x Flow clock's X axis is not computable for Thailand at all (only 2 of 5 structure components can ever exist against a >=3 requirement): data/clock-th.json has x = null and quad = 'warmup' for all 141 quarters by design. Thailand's usable instrument is the Compass, not that clock.

The cross-sectional xc block for Thailand carries vacancy = 18 from data/markets-summary.json. That is a 2026 snapshot derived from AREA's unsold-stock figure in a different reference frame -- it is NOT a quarterly series and must never be used to fill the missing supply gauge or to switch the glut warning on.

regression_guard_five_markets.method: byte comparison (cmp) of data/{clock,compass}-{us,tw,my,jp,au}.json against a copy taken before any change

self_checks.au_th_engine_equivalence: The unmodified HEAD version of build_compass.py and the Thailand-enabled version produce byte-identical output for all five existing markets, confirming the MKTS/RAWF/warn changes are inert for them.
self_checks.pre_existing_xc_drift_found: Rebuilding all markets today would change every market's xc block, because data/markets-summary.json was updated in commit 03a7a79 (Thailand's yield 6.5->5.0, mortgageRate 7.00->7.38, populationGrowth 0.5->-0.2, priceIncomeRatio 21->19) after the compass files were last generated, which moves the 12-market cross-sectional medians. This drift is PRE-EXISTING and independent of adding Thailand to MKTS (verified with the HEAD script). It was NOT accepted here: the five existing markets' files were restored byte-identical and only data/compass-th.json was written (build_compass.py now takes an optional market-name argv filter for exactly this).

th_holdout.verdict: Thailand's four-cell ordering HOLDS, and more strongly than any market except Malaysia: rho = 0.527 over 111 scored quarters (1995Q3-2023Q1), 5/6 declared pairs concordant, with fuelled the best cell (median 18.8% 3y forward, n=29) and starved the worst (median 7.1%, n=49). The single inversion is draining (7.3%, n=24) below reflating (11.0%, n=9) -- reflating is the thinnest cell in the sample. The result survives the overlap correction directionally (non-overlapping median rho 0.483, all three offsets positive, n=9-10 each) and both era halves (pre-2010 0.424, post-2010 0.697). Unlike Australia's hold-out, this is a positive out-of-sample result for the ORDERING claim only. It says nothing about the risk gauge, which is NOT EVALUABLE for Thailand because the supply-glut term does not exist -- and it must not be read as evidence that Thailand carries no supply risk: the supply state is UNKNOWN TO THIS ENGINE, while the site's own market report documents a severe Bangkok glut.
